summary: The archive mailbox is operational on node1 through Dovecot. Node2 authenticated with the dedicated demonstration credential and verified both messages, Message-ID values, bodies, and read/unread states. The staged source remains intact, and both nodes passed sequential restart-persistence checks without changing the OS release or kernel.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL 10-compatible Dovecot 2.3.21 package on node1.
Created the dedicated archive account and a node-generated demonstration password supplied only through secret environment handling.
Copied the staged messages into a separate live Maildir, encoding one.eml as read and two.eml as unread.
Enabled Dovecot, exposed IMAP through firewalld, and verified the listener on port 143.
Authenticated from node2 and retrieved both messages using read-only IMAP operations.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially, verified changed boot identities, and revalidated service and data health after each restart.
Confirmed the original staged mailbox and mailbox.tsv remain intact by comparing final SHA-256 hashes with the initial baseline.

evidence.requirement: Working IMAP service for the archive account on node1
evidence.summary: Dovecot is enabled, active, listening on port 143, and accepts archive-account authentication from node2.

evidence.requirement: Both messages preserve Message-ID values, bodies, and read/unread state
evidence.summary: Node2 retrieved exactly two messages: <one@branch.test> with body 'Shipment arrived.' and Seen=true, and <two@branch.test> with body 'Shipment departed.' and Seen=false.

evidence.requirement: The sole staged mailbox copy remains intact
evidence.summary: Initial source hashes match imported content hashes, and final source hashes remain unchanged, including mailbox.tsv.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained with compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64; Dovecot came from the RHEL 10 repository.

Healthy baseline boot ID d9f8550d-... was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to 32e7d147-..., and service, listener, hashes, staged source, and remote retrieval all recovered.
Healthy baseline boot ID 4ebdfa06-... was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to 045ad47e-..., and node2 again authenticated and verified both messages and flags.
